questions.prompt: A leader in term 7 receives an AppendEntries reply carrying term 9. What does it do?
options: Sets currentTerm to 9 and becomes a follower
Ignores the reply because only requests can change its term
Increments its term to 10 and starts a new election
questions.explanation: Any request or response with a higher term makes a server adopt that term and revert to follower. Starting an election is tempting but wrong: there may already be a perfectly good leader in term 9, and the stale leader should wait for it rather than disrupt it.

questions.prompt: Why must votedFor be written to stable storage before a server replies to RequestVote?
options: So the leader can audit how each server voted
So a restarted server cannot vote for a different candidate in the same term, which could produce two leaders
Because the election timeout is stored alongside it
It does not need to be; only the log must be persisted
questions.explanation: If the vote were only in memory, a crash and restart would let the server vote again in the same term. Two candidates could then each assemble a majority, violating Election Safety. The log alone is not enough, which is why currentTerm and votedFor are also persistent.

questions.prompt: Which state can a Raft server safely lose in a crash?
options: The log entries it has acknowledged
questions.explanation: commitIndex can be relearned from the leader and lastApplied restarts at 0 with the state machine rebuilt from the log or snapshot. The other three are the persistent state listed in Figure 2, and losing any of them can break safety.

diagrams.title: Raft server roles and transitions
diagrams.source:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Follower : starts up
    Follower --> Candidate : election timeout, no leader heard
    Candidate --> Candidate : election timeout, split vote, new term
    Candidate --> Leader : receives votes from a majority
    Candidate --> Follower : discovers current leader or higher term
    Leader --> Follower : discovers server with higher term
